title: Sentry Shift Procedures and Dependency Timeline — Sprint 12 Safety Draft
body:
Purpose
This doc is a working draft for the weekend/overnight sentry shifts and the attached dependency timeline for Sprint 12. It focuses on safe traffic ramp, observable signal thresholds, and explicit ownership for each dependent subsystem. The goal: reduce cognitive load for on-call engineers and give a single source-of-truth for decisions during the first 72 hours of the release window.

Scope
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated gateway changes deployed between 2026-05-08 00:00 UTC and 2026-05-10 23:59 UTC.
- Includes runtime kernel selector change, autoscaler tuning, and two minor model weights roll (v1.12.3 -> v1.13.0).
- Excludes private deployments and per-customer instance updates.

Quick operating summary
- Preflight window: May 6–7 (staging smoke & perf).
- Deploy window: May 8 00:00 UTC — May 9 06:00 UTC (main push).
- Ramp window: May 9 06:00 UTC — May 10 18:00 UTC (traffic ramping to 100%).
- Sentry coverage: 24h active monitoring first 72h after main push with 3-hour overlap between core shift leads.

Preflight checklist (must be green before the main push)
- [ ] Staging perf run: baseline token throughput vs canary (run id: perf-run-2026-05-06-17). Compare p95 latency and cost/sample.
- [ ] End-to-end smoke: request/response path validated for text-generation, chat streaming, and embeddings. (Smoke script v3.2)
- [ ] KV cache migration dry-run: simulate warm cache conditions with representative prefix set.
- [ ] Autoscaler policy sanity: verify min/max pods and burst behavior in staging.
- [ ] Metrics export: ensure new kernel-selection metrics are present (kernel_choice, kernel_latency_ms).
- [ ] Telemetry retention: verify 7-day retention buffer for release traces and sampling rules.
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed and assigned.

Dependency timeline (owners and hard windows)
- infra/gke-autoscaler: Diego Rivera — freeze changes after May 7 12:00 UTC. Any infra edits must be coordinated via #infra-deploys.
- model-serving: Marta Kowalczyk — model weight push May 8 01:00–02:00 UTC (canary segment first).
- routing/proxy: Evan Ross — gradual route update May 9 06:00–10:00 UTC, start at 2% traffic.
- observability/pipeline: Samira Ahmed — ensure trace and log processing scaling enabled May 7 18:00 UTC.
- third-party auth (SAML provider): Priya Narang — contact window May 6–9 in case of SSO regression.

Sentry shift roster and responsibilities
- Shift structure: 8-hour blocks, primary + secondary on-call; primary triages alerts, secondary handles mitigation tasks and scripted rollbacks.
- Day 0 (deploy day) coverage: 00:00–08:00 UTC (Priya), 06:00–14:00 UTC (Evan overlap), 12:00–20:00 UTC (Marta overlap)
- Day 1 coverage: 00:00–08:00 UTC (Diego), 08:00–16:00 UTC (Samira), 16:00–00:00 UTC (Priya)
- Communication: use Slack runbook thread, update incident timeline doc when taking manual action. Notify customer-facing CS lead if degradation > 5% customer-impacting requests.

Signal thresholds (primary automatic gating)
- Latency: p50 baseline + 30% and p95 baseline + 25% over a 5m sliding window => page.
- Error rate: 0.5% elevated over baseline for 10m => alert. 1.5% => page and consider immediate rollback.
- 5xx count: > 100 errors across region in 10m => page SRE and release lead.
- Token generation divergence: model output QA regression: fail rate > 2% on canonical prompt set (eval-run id: canary-eval-2026-05-08) => hold ramp.
- Observability gaps: missing kernel_choice metric or missing traces for > 15m => page observability owner.

Manual escalation rubric
- If any gating threshold triggers, primary should immediately:
  1) Switch canary back to baseline model variant (metric: model_variant_switch_time).
  2) If sustained error > 1% after 15m, abort rollout and flip traffic to pre-deploy traffic table.
  3) Open incident and start timeline in Incident Doc template.
  4) Notify CS and Sales if rollback is likely to affect customers.

Soft-launch ramp plan (traffic percentages and durations)
- Phase A (canary): 2% for 30m. If p95 and error gates OK, proceed.
- Phase B: 10% for 45m. Re-evaluate KV cache hit rates and latency shifts.
- Phase C: 25% for 90m. Observe cross-region parity.
- Phase D: 50% for 3h. Monitor sustained backend load and autoscaler behavior.
- Phase E: 100% after all signals green for 3h at 50% and no unblockers.

Rollback decision matrix (simple)
- Soft failure (latency spike with no error increase): hold and observe for 2x measurement window (typically 10m).
- Medium failure (error rise 0.5–1.5%): partial rollback to 25% traffic while investigation continues.
- Severe failure (error > 1.5% or > 3xx 5xx flood): immediate rollback to previous stable model and route config.

Release notes (draft)
- Release label: sprint12-safety-2026-05
- Highlights:
  - Kernel selection heuristic improved to prefer fused attention kernels for medium-length sequences; expected 8–12% p95 latency reduction on avg.
  - Autoscaler policy change: reduced cooldown from 3m -> 90s for bursty tail latency workloads.
  - Model bump: baseline LM model weights v1.12.3 -> v1.13.0 (minor quality fixes for punctuation handling).
- Deprecated: legacy prefix-caching disabled by default for new deployments (flag: --legacy-prefix-cache=false).
- Known issues:
  - Rare tokenization edge case remains for certain East Asian punctuation sequences; mitigation: fallback to v1.12.3 via model_variant param.
  - Observability: some kernel_choice samples may be missing for the first 30m after cold starts (investigation ticket: ENGOBS-887).

Post-release follow-ups (owners + deadlines)
- 24h: perf digest (p50/p95/p99) by Diego (due May 10 23:59 UTC).
- 48h: quality regression sweep on canonical prompts by Marta (due May 11 23:59 UTC).
- 72h: final go/no-go summary to Product and CS by Priya (due May 12 23:59 UTC).
- 7 days: update ops runbook with any manual mitigations used during rollout (owner: Samira).

Open questions (to resolve before deploy)
- Do we have an emergency fast-path to swap storage-backed model variants in < 3m if the model registry API becomes slow? (Action: Diego to prototype switcher.)
- Should we temporarily increase trace sampling rate for the first 6h of ramp? (Recommendation: yes at 5% global sample.)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally concise — expand the incident templates if you expect longer postmortems.
- If you modify the dependency timeline, update the "linked_artifacts" list with PRs or run ids.

Appendix: quick commands
- rollback to stable model variant: ./scripts/route-switch --to stable --reason "post-deploy-rollback"
- bump trace sampling: infra/ops toggle trace_sampling=0.05 --scope=release-s12
- run local smoke: scripts/smoke-all.sh --env=staging --run-id=local-$(date +%s)

End of draft. Add comments inline or tag owners for sections you expect them to action.
